item.title: Deploy local AI via Ollama, Open-WebUI and VSCode/VSCodium
item.description:
This is a guide how to install ollama on Linux and serve it to a localhost WebUI (no exposure to the internet) and use Ollama as a Chat Agent in VSCodium.

  • no root / sudo required
  • no proxy server, only conda and python
  • in the following replace USERNAME with your actual username

Install Ollama

Create the Directory structure

mkdir -p /home_local/$USER/ollama/{bin,lib,logs,models,webui}

  • bin/: Stores the Ollama executable.
  • lib/: Holds necessary libraries and dependencies.
  • logs/: Keeps tracking and server logs.
  • models/: Stores downloaded LLMs (Llama, Mistral, etc.).
  • webui/: Reserved for the frontend user interface.

Download and Move the Binary

# Download the latest binary
curl -L https://ollama.com/download/ollama-linux-amd64 -o /home_local/$USER/ollama/bin/ollama

# Make it executable
chmod +x /home_local/$USER/ollama/bin/ollama

Add paths to bashrc

nano ~/.bashrc

item.title: Avoid Python Package Import-Errors in VSCodium or VSCode
item.description:
If you are working with Conda environments, you might notice that VSCodium or VS Code shows “import not found” errors (red squiggly lines) even though your code runs perfectly fine in the terminal.

This happens because the IDE’s Python extension doesn’t automatically know which Conda environment to use for its background linting and IntelliSense. By explicitly setting the interpreter path, you tell the IDE exactly where to look for your installed packages.

item.title: Tune VSCodium for Python
item.description:
VSCodium is the Open-Source binaries version of the popular Visual Studio Code IDE, mainly developed by Microsoft.

However, VSCodium lacks some nice features such as code auto complete, nice code coloring, funtcion preview at howver, etc. The good news is: You can easily enhance your VSCodium Experience, by following the following steps.
